title: Separated finite-type unramified parameter for labelled stable isomorphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $n\ge0$, and let $(W,s_1,\ldots,s_n)$ and $(W',s'_1,\ldots,s'_n)$ be stable pointed curves over $S$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. Fix a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For an $S$-scheme $T$, write $W_T=W\times_ST$ and $W'_T=W'\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and write $s_{i,T},s'_{i,T}$ for the pulled-back sections. The functor sending $T$ to the $T$-isomorphisms $u:W_T\xrightarrow{\sim}W'_T$ satisfying $u\circ s_{i,T}=s'_{\sigma(i),T}$ for all $i$ is represented by an $S$-scheme $J_\sigma$ that is separated, of finite type, and unramified [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism]. The representing bijections commute with pullback along every morphism of $S$-schemes and provide a universal labelled isomorphism. The index set has one permutation if $n=0$; the functor includes arbitrary disconnected and nonreduced test schemes.

source.place: Agent assembly of Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), scheme realization by projective graphs; closed marking equalizers; curves.tex Tags 0E67 (lemma-smooth-vector-fields) and 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields); varieties.tex Tag 0B2G (lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified). Marked relative version of the unramified Isom assertion in de Jong 1997 section 3.8; returned proof steps 1--3.

proof.text: Choose affine opens $U$ covering $S$ on which the finite-type quasi-coherent modules presenting both projective-bundle morphisms have finite generators. The affine-presentation lemma supplies closed immersions of the corresponding bundles into finite projective spaces; compose with the closed immersions of $W_U,W'_U$ into those bundles. Thus both restrictions are H-projective. They are flat and finitely presented by restriction of the hypotheses in the stable-pointed definition, and their geometric fibres have dimension one. The opens $U$ are locally Noetherian. Projective morphisms are proper, hence $W_U\to U$ and $W'_U\to U$ are separated; separatedness is target-local, so $W,W'$ are separated over $S$.

source.place: Tags 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective), 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective): finite generators; projective implies proper.

proof.text: On each $U$ apply the projective-curve graph theorem to $W_U,W'_U$. It gives a separated finitely presented $U$-scheme $J_U$ representing all relative isomorphisms, naturally on every test scheme. Its universal graph has invertible projections and gives $u=p_2p_1^{-1}$. Apply the Isom-graph gluing theorem to this open cover and these graph representatives: its hypotheses hold by step 1 and by precisely these natural graph bijections. Obtain a separated finitely presented $S$-scheme $J$ representing the unlabelled Isom functor, with the same formula for its universal isomorphism $u:W_J\simeq W'_J$. In particular $J\to S$ is of finite type: finite presentation includes quasi-compactness, and a finitely presented affine algebra is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), scheme graph realization; schemes.tex Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors).

proof.text: For each $i$, let $a_i,b_i:J\to W'$ be respectively $u\circ s_{i,J}$ and $s'_{\sigma(i),J}$ followed by $W'_J\to W'$. They have the same map to $S$. Define $E_i=J\times_{(a_i,b_i),W'\times_SW',\Delta_{W'/S}}W'$. Since $W'\to S$ is separated, its diagonal is a closed immersion; hence $E_i\to J$ is a closed immersion. Let $J_\sigma=E_1\times_J\cdots\times_JE_n$, with $J_\sigma=J$ for $n=0$. Repeated closed base change and composition make $j:J_\sigma\to J$ a closed immersion. The fibre-product universal property says, for every $T\to J$, that a factorization through $E_i$ exists exactly when $a_i|_T=b_i|_T$, and it is unique. Applying this successively shows that the points of $J_\sigma$ are exactly the desired labelled isomorphisms. This is equality of morphisms, including their structure-sheaf maps, rather than equality only on geometric points. All these equivalences commute with pullback by the same universal property. The restriction of $u$ is the universal labelled isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01KK (definition-separated), diagonal pullback equalizers; morphisms.tex Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion).

proof.text: The closed immersion $j$ is proper, in particular of finite type. Composition with the finite-type map $J\to S$ shows that $J_\sigma\to S$ is of finite type. It is separated as well: the pullback of the closed diagonal $\Delta_{J/S}$ along $j\times_Sj$ is $J_\sigma\times_JJ_\sigma\hookrightarrow J_\sigma\times_SJ_\sigma$. Since a closed immersion is a monomorphism, the first space is $J_\sigma$ and this map is exactly $\Delta_{J_\sigma/S}$. Thus the diagonal is closed by closed-immersion base change. The monomorphism assertion here follows directly from the closed-subscheme description: a map into a closed subscheme, if it exists over a fixed ambient map, is unique.

Fix a geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, an $\Omega$-point $x$ of $(J_\sigma)_\Omega$, and put $R=\Omega[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. The point $x$ is a labelled isomorphism $u_0:C=W_\Omega\simeq W'_\Omega=C'$. Any $R$-point reducing to $x$ is a labelled isomorphism $u_\epsilon:C_R\simeq C'_R$ reducing to $u_0$. The composite $v=(u_0)_R^{-1}\circ u_\epsilon$ reduces to the identity and fixes each constant marking: $v\circ s_{i,R}=(u_0)_R^{-1}\circ s'_{\sigma(i),R}=s_{i,R}$. The stable-curve definition makes $C$ nonempty, proper (by its projective embedding over the field), connected, reduced and nodal of pure dimension one. The marked points $p_i$, images of the sections $s_{i,\Omega}$, are $\Omega$-points of $C$. They are pairwise distinct, since disjoint sections stay disjoint after base change. They are smooth points of $C$: the open relative smooth locus $V\subseteq W$ containing the sections is smooth over $S$, and $V_\Omega\subseteq C$ is smooth over $\Omega$, because a local presentation $A[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ base-changes to $\Omega[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_r)$ and a lifting problem along a thickening of affine $\Omega$-schemes is one over $S$. Its normalization has finitely many smooth projective connected components by the nodal-normalization model. The reduced normalization is by definition the disjoint union of the normalizations $\widetilde C_Z$ of the irreducible components; each summand is integral, hence connected, so the summands are exactly the $C_a$. The definition's special set on $\widetilde C_Z$ (inverse images of the nonsmooth points, which are the nodes, and of the $p_i$) is exactly $E_a$. For these sets, stability gives $2g(C_a)-2+\#E_a>0$: use at least three points for genus zero, at least one for genus one, and $2g-2>0$ for genus at least two. The marked infinitesimal-field theorem therefore says $v=1$. Consequently $u_\epsilon=(u_0)_R$.

source.place: Tags 0E67 (lemma-smooth-vector-fields), 0E68 (lemma-nodal-vector-fields); more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H5 (lemma-action-by-derivations), marked ideal-preservation restriction.

proof.text: By the natural representing bijections in step 3, step 5 says that every dual-number point of every geometric fibre through every $\Omega$-point is the constant one. The geometric tangent criterion applies because $J_\sigma\to S$ is locally of finite type by step 4. It gives that $J_\sigma\to S$ is unramified. Empty fibres satisfy the criterion vacuously. For $n=0$ the single permutation and empty intersection used above give exactly the unpointed functor; stability still excludes genus-zero components with fewer than three branches and genus-one components with no special point. No step restricts the connectedness or reducedness of $T$: step 3 represents the equations on every $S$-scheme, while dual numbers are used only to test unramifiedness.
